h1: The Institution of the Eucharist: Fifth Luminous Mystery
intro: A little read-aloud book for one decade of the Rosary: The Institution of the Eucharist.
shortAnswer: This book walks children through the Fifth Luminous Mystery, the Institution of the Eucharist: a short story, the Gospel passage, the Our Father, ten Hail Marys and the Glory Be, and a reflection on love of the Eucharist and sacrificial union.
aboutHtml:
Painting: Juan de Juanes, Last Supper. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons. Image source (Wikimedia Commons).

The Gospel passage is quoted word for word from the Douay-Rheims Bible, 1899 American Edition, which is in the public domain; verse numbers are omitted for reading aloud, and … marks skipped verses. The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers follow the standard formulas used across this site. This mystery is traditionally prayed on Thursday.

faq.q: What is the Fifth Luminous Mystery?
faq.a: The Institution of the Eucharist. At the Last Supper, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and said: This is my body. This mystery is traditionally prayed on Thursday, and its fruit is love of the Eucharist and sacrificial union.

faq.q: How do you pray this decade with children?
faq.a: Read one page at a time. On the decade page, pray the Our Father once, the Hail Mary ten times (one for each bead), then the Glory Be and the Fatima prayer.
